notes.meaning: God reminds Israel that the tribe of Levi would not receive a land territory like the other tribes. Instead, they were supported by the sacrifices and offerings the people brought to God's altar. Because the Levites were set apart for sacred service, the Lord Himself was their portion and security.

Whenever an Israelite offered a sacrifice of thanksgiving or fellowship, certain choice parts belonged to the officiating priest. These parts were the shoulder, the cheeks, and the stomach. This rule ensured that the priests were properly fed while carrying out their duties at the sanctuary.

The people were also commanded to bring the priests the very first harvest of their grain, new wine, and olive oil. They even gave the first wool sheared from their sheep so the priests would have clothing. Giving the first and best of their goods showed honor to God by caring for His ministers.

The Lord chose the tribe of Levi and Aaron's family out of all Israel to stand before Him in lifelong service. Their sacred duty was to lead worship and serve the people in God's name. Because God personally appointed them, the community had a lasting duty to honor and support them.

If a Levite living in a distant town had a strong desire to serve full-time at the central place of worship, he was welcomed to do so. He served alongside the other Levites and received an equal share of the sacred meals and offerings. Any money he had from selling personal or family property was his own and did not reduce his daily share.

As Israel prepared to enter the Promised Land, God warned them never to copy the detestable practices of the Canaanite nations. Being God's holy people meant refusing to borrow false forms of worship from the surrounding culture. True religion stays pure by leaving behind pagan customs.

God strictly banned awful rituals like offering children as burnt sacrifices to false gods. He also outlawed all occult arts, including fortune-telling, casting spells, practicing sorcery, and trying to speak with evil spirits or the dead. Seeking supernatural power or secret knowledge from demonic sources is a direct rebellion against God.

Anyone who practices these dark arts is detestable in the eyes of the Lord. In fact, God drove the Canaanite nations out of the land precisely because of these wicked customs. Israel was warned that practicing the same things would bring God's judgment upon them as well.

God told His people to be blameless and wholehearted in their devotion to Him alone. This command required complete separation from all superstition and pagan magic. Their faith had to rest completely on the one true God without compromise.

The heathen nations listened to fortune-tellers and sorcerers to direct their lives, but the Lord forbade Israel from doing so. God had not left His people in darkness to hunt for guidance from spirits. He gave them His own word and truth to guide their steps.

Instead of fortune-tellers, God promised to raise up a true Prophet from among the people, just like Moses. This pointed to the line of true prophets God sent to guide Israel, and it found its highest fulfillment in Jesus Christ. The people were commanded to listen to this Prophet and obey Him.

differ.view: Reformed teachers often view this promise as speaking of a continuous line of prophets sent to Israel, reaching its full completion in Jesus Christ.
Some Baptist writers emphasize that the passage speaks exclusively of Jesus Christ as the singular promised Prophet, rather than a line of prophets.

notes.meaning: Moses reminds the Israelites of the terrifying day at Mount Sinai when God gave the law with thunder, fire, and smoke. The people had begged not to hear God's terrifying voice directly so that they would not die, asking instead for a human mediator to stand between them and God. The Lord praised their request and agreed to communicate with them through a human messenger.

The Lord reaffirmed His promise to send a Prophet who would be an Israelite like Moses. God promised to put His exact words into the Prophet's mouth, and the Prophet would speak only what God commanded. Jesus later fulfilled this completely, saying that all His teachings came directly from the Father.

God warned that He would personally hold accountable anyone who refused to listen to this Prophet. Rejecting the words spoken in God's name was the same as rejecting God Himself. Those who turn away from God's chosen messenger face His certain judgment.

Any prophet who claimed to speak in the Lord's name without being commanded, or who spoke for other gods, was guilty of treason against the Almighty. Because spiritual lies could mislead the entire nation into ruin, God ordered that such a false prophet be put to death. No one was allowed to invent their own messages and claim they came from heaven.

God gave the people a clear test to tell whether a message really came from Him. If someone claimed to speak in the Lord's name and their prediction failed to come true, the Lord had not spoken through them. The people did not need to fear such false prophets or be intimidated by their threats.
